app.name: Who knows best?
app.tagline: Myth or truth. You have seconds to decide.

welcome.eyebrow: A card game about what is true
welcome.lead: One statement, a few seconds. Call it true or call it a myth before anyone else at the table does.
welcome.heroCard: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
welcome.tryLead: A real card from the deck. Green means you were right. What the statement turned out to be is a separate question, and it gets its own colour.
welcome.deckLead: Every category is printed with its own mark, so you know what you are being asked about before you have finished reading the card.
welcome.roomTitle: Bring friends, or bots that answer like people
welcome.roomBody: Share a six character code and play the same deck at the same moment. Empty seats take bots that answer at human speed and get things wrong the way people do.
welcome.roomSeats: Two to eight players to a room.
welcome.recordBody: Every match feeds your statistics, your level, and a leaderboard that does not forget.
welcome.languagesBody: The interface and the cards, in whichever you read fastest. The table is lit or dark, and either can change mid match.

science.statement: We only use ten percent of our brains.
science.fact: Imaging shows activity across virtually the whole brain, including during sleep.

space.statement: Neptune was found by mathematics before anyone looked for it.
space.fact: Its position was predicted from wobbles in Uranus's orbit, then confirmed within a degree.

history.statement: Vikings wore horned helmets into battle.
history.fact: Not one has been found in a Viking grave. The horns come from a 19th century opera costume.

sports.statement: An Olympic gold medal is mostly silver.
sports.fact: Silver, with about six grams of gold on the outside. The last solid gold was awarded in 1912.

geography.statement: The summit of Everest is the point furthest from the centre of the Earth.
geography.fact: That is Chimborazo, in Ecuador. The planet bulges at the equator.

arts.statement: Van Gogh sold almost nothing while he was alive.
arts.fact: One confirmed sale, The Red Vineyard, against some nine hundred paintings.

technology.statement: Deleting a file wipes it from the disk straight away.
technology.fact: It normally just drops the entry. The bytes sit there until something overwrites them.

culture.statement: The wedding ring sits on the left hand because Rome believed a vein ran from it to the heart.
culture.fact: The vena amoris. The anatomy was wrong, but the custom outlived it.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: WKB is a student project built for the 42 curriculum. This page explains exactly what the application stores about you, why it stores it, and how to get rid of it. It is written to be read, not to be skipped.

sections.heading: Who runs this service
body: WKB is operated by the student who built it, as coursework for the 42 School ft_transcendence project. It is not a commercial service and there is no company behind it.
For any question about your data, contact the account that hosts the instance you are using.

sections.heading: What we collect
body: Account details: your email address, your display name, the password you chose (stored only as an Argon2id hash, never in readable form), your interface language, and the date you signed up.
Optional profile data: an avatar image, if you upload one.

If you sign in with 42, Google or GitHub: the provider's account identifier, your email address, your name, and your profile picture URL, as supplied by that provider. Signing in with 42 reads only the `public` scope of your intra profile, and the picture stays hosted by 42 rather than being copied here.

Gameplay data: the rooms and matches you take part in, every answer you give with its timing, your scores, your combos, your final placements, your experience points and level, the achievements you unlock, and which facts you have already been shown.
Social data: friend requests you send or receive, and users you block.
Technical data: the timestamp of your last activity, used only to show whether you appear online, and the round-trip latency of your live connection, used to validate reaction times fairly.

sections.heading: Why we collect it
body: To let you sign in and keep you signed in.
To run matches: score answers, keep the scoreboard consistent, and let you reconnect to a match in progress without losing your place.
To make sure you are never shown the same fact twice.
To display your statistics, your match history and the leaderboard.
To validate reaction times, so that a slow connection does not cost you points and a modified client cannot claim an impossible one.

sections.heading: What we never do
body: We do not sell your data, share it with advertisers, or transfer it to any third party.
We do not use analytics or tracking scripts. There are no third-party cookies.
We do not send you marketing email. The application does not send email at all.
We do not profile you beyond the game statistics shown to you on your own profile page.

sections.heading: Cookies
body: One cookie is set: a session refresh token. It is httpOnly, marked Secure, restricted to this site with SameSite=Strict, and scoped to the authentication endpoints only.

A second, short-lived cookie is set only while a 42, Google or GitHub sign-in is in progress, to protect that exchange against cross-site request forgery. It is deleted as soon as the sign-in completes.
Neither cookie is used for tracking, and no cookie is set before you sign in.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
body: Account and gameplay data are kept for as long as the account exists.
Session refresh tokens expire after 30 days, and are revoked immediately when you log out or change your password.
Because this is a coursework project, the database may be reset without notice between evaluation sessions.

sections.heading: Your rights
body: You can view everything the application holds about you from your profile page, and download all of it as a single JSON file under Your data: your account, your statistics, every match and every answer, your achievements and your friends.
You can correct your display name, language and avatar at any time from the same page.

You can delete your account yourself, from your profile page under Your data. It asks you to type your display name back and re-enter your password first, because it cannot be undone. Deleting a user removes their profile, sessions, answers, match participation, friendships and achievements, because every one of those tables cascades on delete.
If you are in the European Union, these correspond to your rights of access, rectification and erasure under the GDPR.

sections.heading: Security
body: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id and a per-password random salt. Nobody, including the operator, can read them.
Session refresh tokens are stored only as keyed hashes, so a copy of the database is not enough to impersonate you.
Every connection between your browser and the server uses HTTPS.
This is a student project and makes no claim to production-grade security. Please do not reuse a password you use anywhere else.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms cover the use of WKB, a student project built for the 42 curriculum. By creating an account you accept them.

sections.heading: What this service is
body: WKB is a real-time multiplayer quiz game. Players are shown a statement and vote on whether it is a myth or the truth, within a time limit. Scores depend on correctness and speed.
It is coursework, provided free of charge, with no guarantee of availability, no support commitment, and no warranty of any kind.

sections.heading: Your account
body: You must provide a valid email address and choose a display name that other players will see.
You are responsible for keeping your password confidential and for everything done through your account.
One person, one account. Do not create accounts to impersonate somebody else.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
body: Choose a display name that is not offensive, and an avatar that is neither offensive nor infringing. The operator may remove either without notice.

Do not attempt to modify the client to gain an advantage. Scoring, timing and card selection are all decided by the server; attempts to forge reaction times are detected and discarded, and repeated attempts may result in the account being removed.
Do not attempt to disrupt the service for other players, overload it, or gain access to accounts that are not yours.

sections.heading: Game content
body: The card set consists of statements of verifiable fact, each traceable to a source reference stored alongside it. It contains no claims about private individuals and no unverifiable rumours.
Mistakes are possible. If you find a card whose stated answer is wrong, please report it to the operator so it can be corrected or deactivated.
Cards are provided for entertainment. Do not rely on them as a source of truth for anything that matters.

sections.heading: Content licence and attribution
body: The card set shipped with this project is released under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International licence (CC BY-SA 4.0). Any redistribution or derivative card set must carry the same licence and the same attribution.

The card-generation tooling included in this repository can additionally build a card set from the Open Trivia Database, which is itself licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Where such content is used, that attribution applies and the share-alike obligation propagates.
The application source code is released separately under the MIT licence; see the LICENSE file in the repository.

sections.heading: Availability and changes
body: The service may be taken down, reset, or changed at any time, including deletion of all accounts and match history.
These terms may be updated. The date at the top of this page shows when they last changed.

sections.heading: Liability
body: The service is provided "as is". To the fullest extent permitted by law, the operator is not liable for any loss arising from its use or unavailability.
Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law.
